headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network tools make Claude Code + Cline dangerous by default for prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write filesystem content, and both support MCP, so one agent can place attacker-controlled instructions where the other may ingest them. Claude Code shares state via filesystem and git; Cline shares via filesystem. This is a plausible default pathway, though not as direct as a shared clipboard or queue.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or repo, injected text can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent treats file contents or MCP output as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Use read-only handoff files between agents.
Require human review before either agent follows instructions found in files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and broad filesystem contents, while Cline can read workspace files and browser screenshots and sends context to a configured model provider. With shared filesystem-based state, sensitive repo data can flow from A into B and then out to third-party inference or browser tooling. The blast radius includes secrets and source code.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets, both agents can access them.
IF Cline forwards workspace context or screenshots to its model provider, those secrets can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspaces.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Disable browser capture when handling sensitive repos.
Rotate exposed credentials after any shared-session use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, git mutation, package installation, and broad network egress. Their shared-state model is filesystem-based, so concurrent edits can collide on the same repo or workspace without locking. That creates a direct conflict over mutable resources and can corrupt git state or overwrite each other's changes.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git branch or working tree concurrently, conflicts can overwrite work.
IF either agent installs packages or runs shell commands in the same environment, side effects can interfere.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Keep package installs out of shared environments.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both agents are autonomous coding tools that can act on files and git state, so one agent's output can become the other's input and then be executed or committed. Claude Code's filesystem/git sharing and Cline's workspace loop make it easy for unverified suggestions to cascade into code changes or browser-driven actions. The default path lacks a built-in verification barrier.
conditions: IF one agent writes a plan, patch, or fact file that the other consumes, errors can propagate.
IF the second agent commits or executes based on the first agent's output without verification, the cascade becomes harmful.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before commits.
Use a separate reviewer agent or human check.
Keep generated plans in non-executable files.
Limit each agent to one task at a time.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents touch source code and files, but Claude Code also handles git credentials and broad filesystem contents while Cline can capture browser screenshots and send context to a configured model provider. If regulated data is present in the workspace, differing logging, retention, or transmission behavior can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not show a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, both agents can process it.
IF Cline's provider or browser tooling retains screenshots or prompts longer than Claude Code's local workflow, retention policies diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Disable screenshot capture for sensitive tasks.
Review provider retention settings before use.
Use separate projects for regulated and unregulated work.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a common retention policy.
